description: A single-panel deformation-mechanism map (strain rate–temperature processing map) for Fe-8% Al ferritic steel. The y-axis is strain rate (s⁻¹) on a logarithmic scale spanning 0.01 to 100 (labelled at 0,01 / 0,1 / 1 / 10 / 100); the x-axis is Temperature (°C) on a linear scale from 850 to 1150 with ticks every 50 °C. The legend at the right defines a large red filled circle as "DDRX activated" and a smaller green filled circle as "DDRX not activated". Experimental points form three vertical columns at 900, 1000 and 1100 °C. Within each column the red (DDRX activated) points occupy the upper strain-rate region (topmost point at 10 s⁻¹, extending down to roughly the 1 s⁻¹ gridline), while the green (DDRX not activated) points lie at the lowest strain rates (near the 0,1 s⁻¹ gridline), with a red point immediately above each green group marking the transition. A heavy dashed curve runs diagonally across the plot, falling from between the 1 and 10 s⁻¹ gridlines at 850 °C to just above the 0,1 s⁻¹ gridline at ~1150 °C; red points lie above this boundary and green points below it at every temperature. The figure demonstrates that the DDRX activation domain is delimited by a critical strain rate that decreases as temperature rises, while lower temperature/low strain-rate conditions fall outside the DDRX field. No numeric values are printed on the points themselves. The group is composite-free: one plot only.
measured_quantities: critical strain rate for DDRX activation (s⁻¹)

observations.observation: The figure is a strain rate versus temperature map; strain rate (s⁻¹) is plotted on a logarithmic y-axis from 0.01 to 100 and Temperature (°C) on a linear x-axis from 850 to 1150 with 50 °C tick spacing.
The legend labels a large red filled circle as 'DDRX activated' and a smaller green filled circle as 'DDRX not activated'.
Data points are arranged in three vertical columns at 900, 1000 and 1100 °C; no points are plotted at other temperatures.

In every column, red 'DDRX activated' points occupy the higher strain rates (topmost near the 10 s⁻¹ gridline) and green 'DDRX not activated' points occupy the lowest strain rates (near the 0,1 s⁻¹ gridline).

A heavy dashed line runs diagonally across the plot from between the 1 and 10 s⁻¹ gridlines at 850 °C down to just above the 0,1 s⁻¹ gridline at about 1150 °C, i.e. the critical strain rate for DDRX activation decreases with increasing temperature.
Red and green points are separated by the dashed boundary at all three temperatures: red above the line, green below it.
No numeric data labels are printed on any point; all values must be read against the log gridlines.
The caption states the figure is a strain rate–temperature map displaying the activation domain of the DDRX mechanism in the Fe-8% Al ferritic steel.
The citing text attributes the map to Castan et al., who studied a ferritic Fe-8 wt.% Al alloy by hot torsion.

The citing text states the hot-torsion tests were performed from 900 °C to 1100 °C with a strain rate range of 0.1–10 s⁻¹, matching the plotted temperature columns and the strain-rate span of the data points.

The citing text states that at high temperature and high strain rate the alloy undergoes discontinuous dynamic recrystallization (DDRX), whereas at lower temperature and low strain rate continuous dynamic recrystallization (CDRX) occurs.

subfigures.description: Log strain rate (s⁻¹) vs temperature (°C) map, y from 0.01 to 100, x from 850 to 1150 °C, with red circles = 'DDRX activated' and green circles = 'DDRX not activated', data in three columns at 900, 1000 and 1100 °C, and a heavy dashed DDRX-boundary curve falling from high strain rate at low temperature to low strain rate at high temperature.
